text: This new website looked amazing. Then the phone stopped ringing.
Kestrel Bay Physio. Made up, but this happens all the time.
For years, their back pain page sat near the top of Google.
Then they launched a shiny new website, and that page got a new address.
But Google was still sending people to the old address, and it didn't exist anymore.
So patients clicked, hit 'Page not found', and booked with someone else.
The fix is called a redirect. A 301 tells Google this page moved, and where it lives now.

text: Before any redesign, list every old page and redirect each one to its new home.
Then check Google Search Console for 'not found' errors in the weeks after launch.
